ContextFreeGrammars.description: Context-Free Grammars visualizer — animated parse trees showing Chomsky hierarchy (regular → context-free → context-sensitive → unrestricted) with leftmost derivation step-by-step.
ContextFreeGrammars.name: Context-Free Grammars
ContextFreeGrammars.qfep_connection: The formal hierarchy of grammars — L-systems are a subset of parallel grammars; this artifact locates where rewriting rules sit in the Chomsky tower.

AnimatedTree.description: Time-sliced L-System interpretation showing organic growth animation
AnimatedTree.name: Animated Tree Growth
AnimatedTree.qfep_connection: Grammar rules as F generating E(S) over time — a tiny production rule unfolds into a branching tree. Branching angle IS the λ parameter: small angle = ordered growth, large angle = sprawling chaos.

CityGenerator.description: Procedural pipe network using orthogonal L-System rules
CityGenerator.name: City Generator

ContextSensitiveTree.description: L-System tree with physics-based environmental awareness and branch pruning
ContextSensitiveTree.name: Context-Sensitive Tree
ContextSensitiveTree.qfep_connection: Context-sensitive rules mean the system's F-model adapts to its environment — branches grow toward light, prune in shadow. Local-to-global coherence: each module responds to context while maintaining grammatical structure.

ForestCompetition.description: Multiple L-System trees with competing growth strategies and health mechanics
ForestCompetition.name: Forest Ecosystem
ForestCompetition.qfep_connection: Competition as multi-agent F-minimization — each tree's growth strategy (its F-model) competes for shared resources. The ecosystem emerges from local growth rules interacting through environmental constraints.

Hilbert3D.description: Space-filling curve visualization demonstrating efficient 3D traversal
Hilbert3D.name: 3D Hilbert Curve
Hilbert3D.qfep_connection: A 1D path that visits every point in 3D space — maximum E(S) coverage from minimum F-description. The curve's grammar rule is tiny; the space it fills is infinite. Recursion as F-compression of complexity.

branching_coral.description: Marine L-system coral colony — multiple shoots with wide branching angles produce organic fan and staghorn forms. Color gradient from deep purple-brown base to bright pink coral tips on a rock base.
branching_coral.name: Branching Coral

dna.default: presence=witness + body=orb is the legacy lineage; every witness multiplier is 1.0.
dna.note: The agent DEMOTED pulse_speed rather than exposing it: the identity named a rate as critical_parameter, but its own justification was about how much room the sphere takes - the rate was a proxy for presence. presence spends part of its delta on radius, which self-cancels under an AABB-fitted camera; judge hush vs witness at a fixed camera.

dark_sphere.description: A simple dark sphere used as an atmospheric and geometric reference. Its silhouette, rotation, and low-emission surface make nearby shifts in scale, position, and lighting easier to perceive. Because it changes very little itself, it stabilizes the viewer's sense of what other transformed objects are doing. It functions as a neutral anchor.
dark_sphere.name: Dark Sphere
dark_sphere.qfep_connection: Transformation often needs an invariant reference to be legible. The sphere stays simple so surrounding changes in S can be felt against it.
dark_sphere.capacity: USE a neutral sphere as a reference for scale, silhouette, and atmospheric change.
interactions: observe the pulsing sphere against transformed geometry
use it as a scale and occlusion reference in the room
compare its stable silhouette with more dynamic artifacts nearby
treat it as an atmospheric marker when reading spatial change

fractal_lsystem_string.description: Visualizes the L-system rewriting process — shows how the axiom string expands through each generation, making the grammar visible as text.
fractal_lsystem_string.name: L-System String Expansion
fractal_lsystem_string.qfep_connection: The F-description made visible: each generation shows the string growing exponentially from a tiny axiom. You see the compression ratio directly — one rule produces pages of instructions.

genetic_tree_sculptor.description: Evolutionary L-system tree that uses genetic algorithm selection to sculpt tree forms — combines grammar-based growth with fitness-driven optimization.
genetic_tree_sculptor.name: Genetic Tree Sculptor
genetic_tree_sculptor.qfep_connection: Evolution as F-search: genetic algorithms explore the space of possible L-system parameters, selecting trees by fitness criteria. Natural selection as a meta-grammar operating on grammars.

grammar_provenance.description: Side-by-side L-system trees from three cultural/historical sources — Lindenmayer 1968 botanical, Islamic geometric subdivision, Aboriginal kinship recursion. Same engine, different axioms, different worlds. Asks: whose grammar?
grammar_provenance.name: Grammar Provenance
grammar_provenance.qfep_connection: The axiom is never neutral — every grammar encodes a worldview. Three F-descriptions produce three radically different E(S) landscapes. The engine is the same; the politics are in the rules.

lsystem_dungeon.description: Procedural dungeon floor plan generated from L-system grammar rules — corridors and rooms emerge from string rewriting, rendered as a miniature architectural model.
lsystem_dungeon.name: L-System Dungeon
lsystem_dungeon.qfep_connection: Architecture from grammar: the dungeon layout emerges from rewriting rules on the XZ plane. Rooms and corridors are emergent properties of the string — spatial E(S) from textual F-description.

lsystem_tree.description: Classic deterministic L-system tree — the foundational teaching example showing how a simple grammar rule produces organic branching structure.
lsystem_tree.name: L-System Tree
lsystem_tree.qfep_connection: The simplest demonstration of F generating E(S): one rule F->F[+F]F[-F]F unfolds a single line into a complex branching tree. Minimal description, maximum emergent structure.

parametric_lsystem.description: L-system with continuous angle and length parameters — branch depth controls parametric decay for organic, naturalistic tree and plant forms. More organic than discrete rules.
parametric_lsystem.name: Parametric L-System

space_filling_curve_gallery.description: Triptych of classic space-filling curves — Hilbert, Peano, and Moore — generated via L-system rules and turtle graphics on a floor display. Curves that visit every point in a 2D region.
space_filling_curve_gallery.name: Space-Filling Curve Gallery
space_filling_curve_gallery.qfep_connection: Space-filling curves achieve maximum E(S) coverage — a 1D line that touches every point in 2D space. The grammar that generates them is minimal (low F); the pattern they produce is total (high E(S)). Dimension-transcending order.

dna.default: comparison=grammars, depth=standard - Hilbert at 4, Peano at 3, Moore at 3, side by side with separators and three captions, which is pixel-for-pixel the triptych the 4 existing placements already show
dna.was: the gallery was always three grammars at one fixed depth: the iteration counts 4/3/3, the three x offsets and the caption row were hard-coded inside _generate_texture and _add_labels

lindenmayer_tube_tree.name: Lindenmayer Tube Tree
lindenmayer_tube_tree.description: Walkable L-system plant rendered as volumetric tubes. Uses commons/lsystem_grammar/ substrate — the same DNA that seeds the chandelier, the wind-collapsed softbody, and the Bauhaus primitive version in the research galleries. Circle it in VR to see branch tapering from width_shrink in action.

modulor_cypress.name: Modulor Cypress
modulor_cypress.description: Walkable composition of TWO substrates: L-system plant produces the branching skeleton, Modulor-fold drops a golden-ratio-scaled cone at every leaf tip. Walkable twin of gg_ls02_plant_modulor_folded from the graph-grammar gallery. Circle it to see how composition of grammars produces density.

axiom_bench.name: Axiom Bench (rules -> a plant)
axiom_bench.description: A bench: the axiom and the production rules on panels, and the small tree those few rules grow. The whole plant is in the rules, not the picture.

axiom_room.name: Axiom Room (the plant is in the rules)
axiom_room.description: A room: the production rules as giant wall panels, a tall tree grown from them in the centre.

generations_bench.name: Generations Bench (1..4)
generations_bench.description: The same L-system at iterations 1,2,3,4 in a row - the tree growing generation by generation. Every symbol rewrites at once.

generations_room.name: Generations Room (sprout to tree)
generations_room.description: A walk past five pedestals, each a later generation - sprout to full tree.

growth_animator.name: Growth Animator (watch it grow)
growth_animator.description: A device that animates the L-system growing, rebuilding the tree at the next iteration on a timer.

grammar_bench.name: Grammar Bench (parse tree)
grammar_bench.description: A grammar parsing a string into a branching parse tree. A context-free grammar is a parse tree is a plant.

chomsky_room.name: Chomsky Room (the hierarchy)
chomsky_room.description: Four nested zones - regular, context-free, context-sensitive, recursively-enumerable - each more tangled than the last.

parse_tree_tool.name: Parser (string -> tree)
parse_tree_tool.description: A device that parses an input string into a live parse tree.

turtle_bench.name: Turtle Bench (forward, turn, branch)
turtle_bench.description: A turtle cursor drawing a path from F/+/- commands; the command string and the resulting curve. The grammar is the genotype; the path is the phenotype.

turtle_room.name: Turtle Room (walk the curve)
turtle_room.description: A room-scale turtle path - a big drawn L-system curve you walk along.

turtle_plotter.name: Turtle Plotter (pen on an arm)
turtle_plotter.description: A pen-plotter tracing an L-system curve onto a plate.

koch_loom.name: Koch Loom (edge fabric)
koch_loom.description: The Koch curve as an edge loom, weaving a bolt of Koch-edged fabric. Infinite length around a finite area.

dragon_bench.name: Dragon Bench (order as chaos)
dragon_bench.description: The dragon curve folding into being on a bench - order so deep it reads as chaos.

curve_plotter.name: Curve Plotter (dragon/Levy/Gosper)
curve_plotter.description: A device cycling the classic curves - dragon, Levy C, Gosper - on a timer.

hilbert_bench.name: Hilbert Bench (a line fills a square)
hilbert_bench.description: A 2D Hilbert curve filling a square - one dimension reaching, by recursion, to fill two.

hilbert_room.name: Hilbert Room (one line, every point)
hilbert_room.description: A room-scale 3D Hilbert curve you walk around - a line that visits every point.

bracket_bench.name: Bracket Bench (the tree trick)
bracket_bench.description: A bracketed plant with the push/pop stack visualised. [ ] is where the line becomes a tree.

bracket_room.name: Bracket Room (push, branch, pop)
bracket_room.description: A room-scale bracketed tree, tall and many-branched.

bracket_pruner.name: Branch Pruner (trim by depth)
bracket_pruner.description: A bracketed tree pruned past a depth, clippers on an arm.

lsystem_tree_room.name: L-system Tree Room (a whole tree)
lsystem_tree_room.description: A room-tall L-system tree you walk under - a few rules, a branching angle, a whole tree.

tree_nursery.name: Tree Nursery (grow them)
tree_nursery.description: A nursery of pots, each growing a different L-system tree.

fern_bench.name: Fern Bench (the frond)
fern_bench.description: A Barnsley-style fern on a bench - the leaf is the plant is the frond, self-similar all the way down.

fern_room.name: Fern Room (self-similarity)
fern_room.description: A room of ferns of varied size - self-similarity all the way down.

fern_press.name: Fern Press (pressed flat)
fern_press.description: A botanical press: a fern flattened between glass plates.

coral_bench.name: Coral Bench (greedy local rule)
coral_bench.description: A 3D branching coral - branching is cheaper than planning.

coral_room.name: Coral Room (the reef)
coral_room.description: A coral-reef room of varied corals.

vine_grower.name: Vine Trellis (climbing rule)
vine_grower.description: A trellis with an L-system vine climbing it.

stochastic_toy.name: Stochastic Toy (same seed, same plant)
stochastic_toy.description: A held stochastic plant: random rule choice, but the same seed always grows the same plant.

stochastic_bench.name: Stochastic Bench (no two alike)
stochastic_bench.description: Several plants from different seeds, same rules - no two the same. Randomness makes a population, not a clone.

stochastic_room.name: Stochastic Room (a meadow)
stochastic_room.description: A meadow of stochastic plants, every one different.

stochastic_seeder.name: Stochastic Seeder (a new plant each time)
stochastic_seeder.description: A seeder growing a new random plant on a timer.

parametric_bench.name: Parametric Bench (numbers on symbols)
parametric_bench.description: A tree that tapers and widens by depth - hang numbers on the symbols and the grammar can taper, bend, grow old.

parametric_room.name: Parametric Room (taper, bend, grow old)
parametric_room.description: A room-scale parametric tree, trunk to twig.

parametric_designer.name: Parametric Designer (tune the params)
parametric_designer.description: A device re-growing the tree through a parameter sweep.

context_toy.name: Context Toy (a signal up the stem)
context_toy.description: A held context-sensitive plant - a signal passing up the stem, a symbol reading its neighbours.

context_room.name: Context Room (pruned by its world)
context_room.description: A tree pruned by a ceiling/wall - the plant answers its world.

context_pruner.name: Context Pruner (trims at the obstacle)
context_pruner.description: A tree growing against an obstacle, branches near it trimmed.

substrate_bench.name: Substrate Bench (one string, three materials)
substrate_bench.description: The same L-system string as lines, tubes, and a graph, side by side.

substrate_room.name: Substrate Room (the grammar is the DNA)
substrate_room.description: The same string as a tube tree, a graph, a skeleton, on three pedestals. The grammar is the DNA, the material is a choice.

substrate_switcher.name: Substrate Switcher (cycle the material)
substrate_switcher.description: A device cycling the same string between render modes.

city_toy.name: City Toy (a held block)
city_toy.description: A held orthogonal L-system city block - point the rules at right angles instead of leaves.

city_bench.name: City Bench (a street plan)
city_bench.description: An orthogonal L-system street/block layout - the same engine grows a city.

city_room.name: City Room (streets and dungeons)
city_room.description: A room-scale L-system city/dungeon of orthogonal walls you could walk.

sapling_toy.name: Sapling Toy (the start of a forest)
sapling_toy.description: A held young sapling - the grammar becoming biology.

forest_bench.name: Forest Bench (many grammars, one world)
forest_bench.description: A stand of small trees competing for space - many grammars, one world.

grove_room.name: Grove Room (grammar becomes biome)
grove_room.description: A room-scale grove of L-system trees - the grammar becomes the biome that plants it.

grammar_seed.description: The L-systems seam and the compression thesis made literal. This plant is not stored - it is a tiny grammar (axiom + two rewrite rules) expanded a few times and walked by a turtle. A handful of bytes become a forest: a short seed with a costly branching run. The cost of the gift is reproducibility - run the same grammar again and the tree returns leaf for leaf. The organic was a formula.
grammar_seed.name: Grammar Seed
grammar_seed.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for lsystems. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
